name: event-filtering
title: Filter and paginate the events listing
body:
## Motivation

`GET /admin/events` can only filter by status and returns at most the newest 200 events. When finance asked last week for every `refund.created` from Acme in December (PAY-241), the only way to get them was to open the production database, because there were more than 200 events since then and no way to narrow by type or date. Support has asked for the same thing to chase individual refunds. The listing should be filterable and let you walk through everything that matches.

## Changes

- `GET /admin/events` accepts `type`, `provider`, `from` and `to` (on the time we received the event) alongside `status`, plus `cursor` for paging and `orderBy` for sorting (defaults to `received_at DESC`, so the default order is unchanged).
- `type`, `provider` and `status` are enums in the query schema, so a typo is a 400 instead of an empty list. Defaults and what each parameter does are written into the schema.
- The response is now `{ items, nextCursor }`. `nextCursor` is `null` on the last page; otherwise pass it back as `cursor`. The cursor is opaque to clients, so we can change how it works later without breaking anyone.
- `limit` still defaults to 50. I dropped the 200 cap, since with paging the client decides how much it wants per page, and finance's export script wants big pages.
- The `WHERE` clause is built from only the filters that are set, so SQLite can use an index for them. New migration adds `events_provider_type ON events (provider, type)`, which covers the provider + type lookups that support and finance actually run.
- README documents the new parameters.

## Testing

- New `app.inject` tests: filtering by type and provider, walking all pages of five events with `limit=2` and checking every event comes back once and in order, and 400s for an unknown provider and a malformed cursor.
- Ran finance's December query against a copy of the production database locally (`provider=acme&type=refund.created&from=2025-12-01&to=2026-01-01`), and paged through it with `limit=500`.
- Existing tests unchanged and passing; `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint` and `pnpm test` are green.

## Open questions

- Should `from` / `to` filter on `received_at` (when we got the webhook) or on the provider's `created` timestamp inside the payload? Finance thinks in terms of when the refund happened at Acme, which can differ by a few minutes when Acme retries. I went with `received_at` because it is a column; filtering on the payload would mean a generated column.
